summary.text: Don Tracy is the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Illinois. A Springfield attorney, he chaired the Illinois Gaming Board from 2015 to 2019 and the Illinois Republican Party beginning in 2021. He says he is running to represent all 102 Illinois counties and focuses on the cost of living.

paragraphs.text: Born in Urbana, Illinois; says he was raised in Mt. Sterling and raised his own family in Springfield.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Arizona State University and a law degree from the University of Memphis.
Says he began working in his family's business at age 10 and later ran a small business.
Is an attorney at the Springfield law firm Brown, Hay & Stephens, where WGLT reported in 2021 that he was a partner.

Chaired the Illinois Gaming Board from February 2015 until June 2019, during Gov. Bruce Rauner's administration. He resigned after the state Office of Executive Inspector General reported that he had engaged in improper political activity by making several campaign contributions while serving on the board, in violation of the Riverboat Gambling Act.
Was named chairman of the Illinois Republican Party in February 2021, succeeding Tim Schneider; he was the first party chairman since 1988 not from Chicago or the collar counties.
Says he has served on boards including the Abraham Lincoln Association and the Sangamon County Bar.
